_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::brownian_dynamics#0. The entry's Signal (mean-square displacement scaling) is an ensemble statement not readable from one 4C run, so this fixture certifies the operational consequence instead, which is the thing that actually catches people: a thermal run does not step-converge, so the usual halve-dt-and-see test is meaningless and will let you accept any dt. Five arms on upstream beam3r_line2_backweuler_browndyn_periodic_rve_dirich_element.4C.yaml at fixed end time and fixed RANDSEED. With KT = 0 the transverse displacement of node 2 moves by 7e-17 between dt = 1e-2 and 5e-3, i.e. the deterministic run does converge. With KT > 0 the same quantity reads 1.97729908169594938e-02, 1.41182827349665852e-02 and -9.93856384578826677e-04 at dt = 1e-2, 5e-3, 2.5e-3: it moves by more than its own size and changes sign. Refining dt draws a different realisation, it does not converge the trajectory; dt must be judged against the physical relaxation time. The refined cold arm still trips one test on the AXIAL component, which is prescribed-ramp sampling error, not noise, so the comparison uses dispx only. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.

_mutation.note: take the temperature away from the finest thermal arm. It then coincides with the deterministic run, the sign flip and the large refinement change disappear, THERMAL_RUN_STEP_CONVERGES flips to yes and the fixture must go red.

stop refining: give every thermal arm the same step. All three then produce the identical realisation, the refinement changes collapse to zero and THERMAL_RUN_STEP_CONVERGES flips to yes, so the fixture must go red.
